# @mission-platform/breakpoints

Responsive breakpoint utilities and **write-once** viewport components for Mission Platform. The components (`ForgeShowAt`, `ForgeHideAt`, `ForgeBreakpointDebug`) are authored once in the neutral `@mission-platform/forge-jsx` dialect and compiled to **both Vue 3 and React** by `@mission-platform/vite-plugin-forge`.

## Subpath Exports

- `@mission-platform/breakpoints/vue` — compiled native Vue 3 components.
- `@mission-platform/breakpoints/react` — compiled native React components.
- `@mission-platform/breakpoints/core` — framework-agnostic utilities and types (`breakpointKeys`, `breakpoints`, `getBreakpointValue`, `mediaQuery`, `maxMediaQuery`, `resolveBreakpoint`, `BreakpointKey`, `BreakpointValues`).
- `@mission-platform/breakpoints` — the neutral JSX source barrel (compiled by `@mission-platform/vite-plugin-forge`).

## Features

### Breakpoint Scale

The following constants are exported for direct use:
- `breakpointKeys` — An array of all available breakpoint keys: `['2xs', 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', '2xl']`
- `breakpoints` — A mapping of keys to their min-width pixel thresholds.

Seven-step responsive scale based on viewport width:

- `2xs` — extra-extra-small: ≥ 0 px (effectively 0)
- `xs` — extra-small: ≥ 480 px
- `sm` — small: ≥ 768 px (tablet portrait)
- `md` — medium: ≥ 1024 px (tablet landscape / small laptop)
- `lg` — large: ≥ 1920 px (Full HD / 1080p)
- `xl` — extra-large: ≥ 2560 px (QHD)
- `2xl` — extra-extra-large: ≥ 3840 px (4K UHD)

### Core Utilities (`/core`)

The Vue-only `useBreakpoints` composable has been **removed**. Build custom reactive viewport logic on the framework-agnostic `/core` helpers with your framework's own hooks (e.g. `apps/service-monitor`'s React `useCompactViewport`, built on `maxMediaQuery`).

### Utility Functions

- `mediaQuery(key)` — Returns a `min-width` media query string: `'\`(min-width: ${value}px)\`'`
- `maxMediaQuery(key)` — Returns a `max-width` media query string for upper-bound
- `getBreakpointValue(key)` — Returns the pixel threshold for a breakpoint
- `resolveBreakpoint(width)` — Given a pixel width, returns the active breakpoint key

### Components

#### `<ForgeShowAt>`

Conditionally renders slot content when the viewport meets specified breakpoint criteria.

```vue
<template>
  <ForgeShowAt min="md">
    <p>This is visible on medium screens and above</p>
  </ForgeShowAt>

  <ForgeShowAt min="sm" max="lg">
    <p>This is visible only on small and medium screens</p>
  </ForgeShowAt>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ForgeShowAt } from '@mission-platform/breakpoints/vue'
</script>
```

**Props:**
- `min?: BreakpointKey` — Show content when viewport is at or above this breakpoint
- `max?: BreakpointKey` — Show content when viewport is strictly below this breakpoint

#### `<ForgeHideAt>`

Conditionally hides slot content when the viewport meets specified breakpoint criteria.

```vue
<template>
  <ForgeHideAt min="lg">
    <p>This is hidden on large screens and above</p>
  </ForgeHideAt>
</template>
```

**Props:** Same as `<ForgeShowAt>`

#### `<ForgeBreakpointDebug>`

Development utility component that displays the current breakpoint in the corner of the screen.

```vue
<template>
  <ForgeBreakpointDebug />
</template>
```

### SCSS Utilities

The breakpoint SCSS layer (variables, `bp-up`/`bp-down`/`bp-between`/`bp-only` mixins, and the
`.bp-show-*`/`.bp-hide-*`/`.bp-only-*` visibility utility classes) now lives in
`@mission-platform/tokens`, alongside the other design-token SCSS. Import it from there:

```scss
// The $breakpoints map + mixins only (no emitted CSS):
@use '@mission-platform/tokens/scss/breakpoints-mixins' as bp;

.container {
  @include bp.bp-up('md') {
    max-width: 1024px;
  }
}

// The .bp-show-*/.bp-hide-*/.bp-only-* visibility utility classes (emits CSS):
@use '@mission-platform/tokens/scss/breakpoints-utilities';
```

This package exports the framework-agnostic `/core` utilities and the write-once components
(`<ForgeShowAt>`, `<ForgeHideAt>`, `<ForgeBreakpointDebug>`) — imported from `@mission-platform/breakpoints/vue`
or `@mission-platform/breakpoints/react` — described above.
